heard: Your headphones don't block noise. They make more of it. Tiny microphones on the outside listen to every sound around you. A chip takes that sound wave and flips it upside down. Then, the speaker plays the flipped wave straight into your ear. Peak meets valley, the two waves cancel, and you hear almost nothing. But there's a catch. It works best on steady low sounds, like the hum of a plane engine. You see, a steady hum repeats so the chip can keep matching it. A sudden voice changes too fast and slips right through. That's why the padding matters. It blocks the high sounds the chip can't. So the silence you paid for is really two noises fighting.
